note: 수동 큐레이션. 공식 발표·공연장·예매처를 교차 확인해 사실을 자체 작성한 것이며 전수 목록이 아니다. 지난 공연은 자동으로 숨겨진다. intl=true 는 내한공연 섹션에 노출. 가격·시간은 발표 시점 기준이라 예매 전 공식 확인 필요.

items.title: PLAVE World Tour: KEEP IT MANIC
items.note: The first virtual idol group to headline Incheon's Munhak Stadium — real members perform as animated avatars via motion capture.
items.overview: PLAVE is a virtual idol boy group: five animated 3-D characters performed live in real time by human members through motion capture, making the show a genuinely unusual fusion of concert and animation with few equivalents anywhere. These Incheon dates open PLAVE's first-ever world tour, a milestone for one of K-pop's fastest breakout acts, and the opener was reportedly moved up to the far larger open-air Munhak Stadium to meet demand — the first time a virtual group has headlined the venue. Expect intense, thriller-themed staging and effects. After Seoul the tour continues to Japan, Taiwan, Thailand, Singapore and Macau.
items.ticketInfo: NOL Ticket (Interpark) — English booking via NOL World (world.nol.com)
items.tip: An open-air stadium show (age 12+) — dress for the weather and take Incheon Subway Line 2 to Munhak Stadium Station, as parking is very limited. If you pay by bank transfer, complete it the same day or the order auto-cancels.

items.title: NCT 127 5th Tour: NEO CITY — SEOUL, THE REDLINE
items.note: SM Entertainment's Seoul-based boy group returns after ~1.5 years, with Taeyong and Jaehyun back from military service.
items.overview: NCT 127 is one of SM Entertainment's flagship boy groups and the Seoul-based unit of the larger NCT project. These three nights open the group's fifth world tour and mark their return after a break of roughly a year and eight months — and, crucially for long-time fans, Taeyong and Jaehyun rejoin the touring lineup after completing mandatory military service, alongside Johnny, Yuta, Doyoung, Jungwoo and Haechan. Expect a large-scale arena production built on the group's signature hard-hitting, experimental 'neo' sound. The final night doubles as a global event, streamed live and screened in cinemas worldwide.
items.showTimes: Sep 18 (Fri) 7:00 PM · Sep 19 (Sat) 5:00 PM · Sep 20 (Sun) 4:00 PM KST
items.ticketInfo: Melon Ticket, with a separate global page for international fans. Sep 19–20 also stream on Beyond LIVE; Sep 20 screens in cinemas worldwide.
items.tip: KSPO Dome is inside Olympic Park — take Subway Line 5 to Olympic Park Station or Line 9 to Hanseong Baekje. If the venue sells out, the Beyond LIVE stream or the Sep 20 cinema broadcast is a reliable fallback. Purchase cap is just 1–2 tickets per person.

items.title: TAEMIN World Tour: LiMiNaL
items.note: Three nights at the Olympic stadium from the SHINee member who has spent fifteen years redefining what a K-pop solo act looks like.
items.overview: Taemin debuted with SHINee in 2008 as the youngest member and has since built a solo career that is taken seriously as dance performance in its own right — closer to a choreographed stage production than a pop concert. The LiMiNaL tour opens with three nights at Jamsil, the main stadium from the 1988 Olympics, which is a statement of scale for a solo artist.
items.showTimes: Sep 18 (Fri) 8:00 PM · Sep 19 (Sat) 6:00 PM · Sep 20 (Sun) 5:00 PM KST · about 2h
items.ticketInfo: YES24 Ticket.
items.tip: Jamsil Sports Complex Station is on Subway Line 2 and sits directly under the venue. The stadium is open-air — September evenings are mild but bring a layer for after dark.

items.title: izna Concert Tour: WHO DAT GIRL?
items.note: The girl group formed on I-LAND 2, on their first headline tour.
items.overview: izna were assembled through I-LAND 2: N/a, the survival show that aired in 2024, and debuted the same year — which makes this first headline tour their proper introduction as a live act rather than a television product. Two nights at Olympic Park.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: Ages 7 and over. Olympic Park is on Subway Line 5 (Olympic Park Station) or Line 9 (Hanseong Baekje).

items.title: ONEWE 6th Live Concert: O! NEW E!volution VI
items.note: A K-pop band that actually plays — guitars, bass, keys and drums, not backing tracks.
items.overview: ONEWE are one of the handful of Korean idol groups built as a live band rather than a dance group, which makes their concerts a different proposition: the arrangements change, the solos are real, and the set runs long. Two nights at KBS Arena for the sixth edition of their own annual show.
items.showTimes: Sep 19 (Sat) 6:00 PM · Sep 20 (Sun) 5:00 PM KST · about 2h 30m
items.ticketInfo: Melon Ticket.
items.tip: Ages 7 and over. KBS Arena is in Gangseo — Subway Line 9 to Yangcheon Hyanggyo, or Line 5 to Balsan. Further west than most venues, so allow extra time from the centre.

items.title: The Fact Music Awards 2026
items.note: A stadium awards night packed with live performances — back in Korea after three years, and in Busan for the first time.
items.overview: The Fact Music Awards (TMA) is one of Korea's big annual K-pop award ceremonies, known for pairing trophies with a stacked lineup of live stages. The 2026 edition returns to Korea for the first time in three years — after being held in Japan (2024) and Macau (2025) — and lands at Busan's open-air Asiad Main Stadium, the host city for the first time. Around 17 acts are confirmed, spanning solo star Lim Young-woong and a broad slate of top idol groups, so it is a chance to see many major artists in a single evening rather than at separate concerts. Confirmed names include RIIZE, ATEEZ, NMIXX, TREASURE, tripleS, ILLIT, CORTIS, xikers, Choi Yena and more.
items.ticketInfo: Yes24 Ticket (English/global page available). Streams globally via CHZZK for those who can't attend.
items.tip: From central Busan, take Subway Line 3 to Sports Complex Station, Exit 7 — about a 20-minute walk to the stadium. An affordable A-tier ticket is a low-cost way to catch a dozen-plus top acts at once.

items.title: Vaundy Asia Arena Tour: HORO in Seoul
items.note: The Japanese artist who writes, produces and designs his own work, on two arena nights near the airport.
items.overview: Vaundy started uploading songs while still at university and now writes, arranges, produces and art-directs almost everything under his own name — 'Odoriko' and 'Kaiju no Hanauta' have both passed the kind of streaming numbers usually reserved for whole labels. The live show moves between rock, funk and ballads without settling, which is roughly how the records work too.
items.showTimes: Sep 19 (Sat) 5:00 PM · Sep 20 (Sun) 4:00 PM KST · about 2h
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: INSPIRE Arena is beside Incheon Airport on Yeongjong Island, not in Incheon city. Allow an hour from central Seoul on the Airport Railroad plus the resort shuttle, and check the last train back before you go.

items.title: OBJET K-POP FESTA 2026
items.note: A two-day, all-ages, full-day K-pop festival at Incheon Munhak Stadium. Lineup is announced closer to the date.
items.overview: OBJET K-POP FESTA is a two-day, all-ages K-pop festival with a long daily runtime — effectively a full-day event with a rotating stage of acts across the weekend. It's held at Incheon Munhak Stadium (per the official Yes24 ticketing pages). The performing lineup is typically revealed in stages, so check the official channels close to the date before planning around specific artists.
items.showTimes: Sep 26 (Sat) & Sep 27 (Sun) — daily schedule announced closer to the event
items.ticketInfo: Yes24 Ticket, with a dedicated English/global page — accepts overseas cards and PayPal
items.price: General ~167,000 · higher grades and 2-day pass up to ~280,000 won (grade names differ between the English and Korean pages — verify at checkout)
items.tip: Use the Yes24 English page and complete passport verification first; PayPal is accepted, which helps if your card is rejected. Incheon Munhak Stadium is on Incheon Subway Line 2.

items.title: Silica Gel Asia Tour: Syn.THE.Size — Ballad of You
items.note: Korea's most acclaimed indie/rock band at their biggest-ever solo shows — the pick for live music beyond idol pop.
items.overview: Silica Gel is one of Korea's most acclaimed indie/rock bands, known for a genre-blurring, psychedelic and electronic-tinged sound and highly visual, art-directed live shows — a very different experience from a mainstream idol concert. These two KSPO Dome nights are billed as the band's largest-ever headline shows, tied to their third album 'Ballad of You,' with a setlist built around the new record. The Seoul concerts launch the band's first Asia tour, continuing to Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur, Taipei, Bangkok and Japan. For an English-speaking visitor who wants live Korean music beyond K-pop, this is a standout — and no lyrics knowledge is needed to enjoy the band's instrumental-heavy sound.
items.showTimes: Sep 26 (Sat) & Sep 27 (Sun) — start times to be confirmed on the ticket page
items.ticketInfo: Interpark / NOL Ticket — English page via NOL World (world.nol.com)
items.price: Seat S 110,000 · Seat R 121,000 · Standing/Seated VIP 143,000 won
items.tip: This is a rock show — the standing-pit ('Standing VIP') tickets put you closest to the energy. Take Subway Line 5 or 9 to Olympic Park.

items.title: TAKUYA KIMURA Live Tour: Checkpoint in Seoul
items.note: The SMAP member and actor, playing an arena show in Korea as a solo musician.
items.overview: Takuya Kimura spent three decades as one quarter of SMAP, the group that defined Japanese pop television, and has been at least as visible since as an actor. The solo live tour is a relatively recent turn, and the Seoul date is a full arena show at INSPIRE. For anyone who grew up with Japanese drama and pop, this is a considerable draw.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: Ages 7 and over. INSPIRE Arena is beside Incheon Airport on Yeongjong Island — an hour from central Seoul on the Airport Railroad plus the resort shuttle.

items.title: Busan International Rock Festival 2026
items.note: Korea's longest-running rock festival, three days on the Nakdong riverbank in Busan.
items.overview: The Busan International Rock Festival has run since 2000 and is the closest thing Korea has to a classic outdoor rock weekend — multiple stages on the flood plain beside the Nakdong River, a mix of Korean bands and international bookings, and a crowd that skews older and more committed than the K-pop festival circuit. It ran free for most of its history and now charges, which has thinned the crowd and improved the experience. Gates open at 11:00 each day and the music runs into the night.
items.ticketInfo: YES24 Ticket. Day tickets are usually sold alongside the three-day pass — check closer to the date.
items.tip: All ages. Samnak Ecological Park is in Sasang, west of central Busan — Subway Line 2 to Sasang, then a bus or a 20-minute walk. It is a river flood plain: bring something to sit on, and shoes you do not mind getting muddy. Pairs well with a Busan trip that uses the old town rather than the beaches.

items.title: Post Malone Live in Seoul
items.note: A stadium show from one of the biggest crossover acts in American music — and the largest international concert on the Korean calendar this autumn.
items.overview: Post Malone arrives in Korea on the back of a career that has moved from hip-hop to pop to, most recently, country — a run of singles including 'Rockstar', 'Sunflower' and 'Circles' that made him one of the most-streamed artists of the last decade. This is a single night at Goyang's 41,000-capacity main stadium, the venue Seoul uses when an arena is not big enough. Ticketing runs the full range from a ₩99,000 seat at the back to VIP packages that clear ₩500,000, so the price you pay depends entirely on how close you need to be.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL). Note this is an 8pm start on a Friday — Goyang is an hour from central Seoul, so plan the return.
items.tip: Ages 19 and over only. The stadium is a 20-minute walk from Daehwa Station, the last stop on Subway Line 3 — trains back into Seoul stop before the crowd clears, so either leave a little early or budget for a long taxi queue.

items.title: &TEAM Tour: BLAZE THE WAY — Seoul Encore
items.note: The Seoul encore of the HYBE Japan group's BLAZE THE WAY tour, over the Chuseok holiday weekend.
items.overview: &TEAM is a HYBE boy group (under HYBE's Japan operation, in the extended ENHYPEN/HYBE family) with a mostly Japanese membership and a strong following across both Japan and Korea. These two KSPO Dome dates are the Seoul encore of their 'BLAZE THE WAY' tour, following the main run held in Incheon earlier in 2026 — encore shows usually fold in the group's newest material and updated staging. The timing lines up with fresh Korean-language releases, so expect recent songs in the set.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark Ticket — mobile tickets only (no paper tickets); English page via NOL World
items.price: General 165,000 · Sound Check 220,000 · Meet & Greet 253,000 won
items.tip: Tickets are mobile-only, so have the Interpark app installed and logged in with a verified account, and keep your phone charged for entry. KSPO Dome is on Subway Line 5/9. Some Japanese is spoken on stage given the group's makeup, but the show is easy to follow without language.

items.title: EDC Korea (Electric Daisy Carnival)
items.note: The Korean edition of the Las Vegas mega-rave, next to Incheon Airport — Tiësto, DJ Snake, Fisher, Alok and more.
items.overview: EDC Korea is the Korean edition of the Las Vegas mega-rave Electric Daisy Carnival: two days of EDM stages at the INSPIRE resort complex on Yeongjong Island, right next to Incheon Airport. The 2026 lineup is headlined by Tiësto, DJ Snake, Fisher, Alok, Subtronics, Sara Landry, SVDDEN DEATH and ILLENIUM B2B DABIN, with stage takeovers from Basscon, Bassrush, Insomniac Records and more. Hotels on site and a direct airport rail link make it one of the easiest festivals in Korea to fly in for.
items.showTimes: Oct 3 (Sat) & Oct 4 (Sun) — set times published in the festival timetable closer to the date
items.ticketInfo: Official site korea.electricdaisycarnival.com; also sold via global travel platforms (Klook, KKday)
items.price: Multi-day and single-day passes — see official site
items.tip: The venue is beside Incheon Airport, so a great option is to fly in and stay at an airport-area or on-site hotel rather than commuting from central Seoul (about an hour away).

items.title: LANY: Soft — Seoul
items.overview: LANY is an American synth-pop trio known for emotive, atmospheric songs like 'ILYSB' and 'Malibu Nights' and a devoted Asian fanbase. This Seoul date, part of their 'Soft' world tour, is a warm, sing-along-heavy indoor show from a band that tours Korea regularly.
items.ticketInfo: NOL Ticket / Live Nation Korea — English via NOL World and livenation.kr/en
items.price: Standing 143,000 · S 154,000 · R 165,000 · P 176,000 won (VIP packages higher)
items.tip: KINTEX is in Ilsan, northwest of Seoul. The fastest route is the new GTX-A express line to Kintex Station; otherwise Subway Line 3 to Daehwa Station (about an hour from downtown).
items.note: American synth-pop trio with a devoted Asian following — an indoor, sing-along-heavy show from a band that tours Korea regularly.

items.title: Gangnam Festival Concert
items.venue: Dosan-daero (in front of Hyundai Motorstudio Seoul)
items.note: A free open-air concert on Dosan-daero headlined by PSY — the 'Gangnam Style' singer in Gangnam itself.
items.overview: The Gangnam Festival closes with a free outdoor concert on Dosan-daero, the boulevard in Sinsa-dong, in front of Hyundai Motorstudio Seoul. The KOPIS listing names PSY, under his legal name Park Jae-sang, as the headline act, with other performers on the bill. PSY's shows are famous for water cannons and non-stop crowd participation, and seeing 'Gangnam Style' performed for free in Gangnam is about as on-theme as a Seoul night out gets. The listing gives an age limit of 15 and over. Expect big crowds and road closures around the stage.
items.ticketInfo: Free — no ticket needed; arrive early for a spot near the stage
items.tip: Sinsa Station (Line 3) and Apgujeong Rodeo Station (Suin-Bundang Line) are both within walking distance. Bring a light rain layer — PSY's sets often involve water.

items.title: Zara Larsson: First Solo Shows in Korea
items.note: The Swedish pop singer's first headline dates in Korea, in a room small enough that it will not stay a secret.
items.overview: Zara Larsson has been making pop singles since she was a teenager in Stockholm — 'Lush Life', 'Never Forget You', 'Symphony' with Clean Bandit — and has kept a foot in dance music throughout. These are her first solo Korean dates, and they are in a 1,000-capacity hall rather than an arena, which is the kind of mismatch that sells out fast.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL). A soundcheck VIP package is sold separately.
items.price: Standing 132,000 · Seated 132,000 · Soundcheck VIP package 347,000 won
items.tip: Ages 15 and over. Myunghwa Live Hall is by Yeongdeungpo Station (Line 1 and the mainline KTX/ITX platforms), so it is easy to reach and easy to leave.

items.title: The Weeknd — Hyundai Card Super Concert
items.overview: The Weeknd is one of the world's biggest pop/R&B stars ('Blinding Lights,' 'Starboy,' 'Save Your Tears'), returning to Korea for the first time in about eight years to headline the large-scale Hyundai Card Super Concert. This is a two-night stadium event expected to draw around 100,000 fans, with Japanese hip-hop duo Creepy Nuts opening.
items.ticketInfo: NOL Ticket — English via NOL World (world.nol.com)
items.price: Roughly 55,000 (restricted view) to 289,000 won; standing 189,000 won
items.tip: Strict 19+ age limit — bring your passport for ID checks. Goyang Stadium is outside central Seoul (nearest is Subway Line 3); for a 100,000-capacity show, plan for heavy post-concert crowds.
items.note: His first Korea show in about eight years, and a two-night stadium run expected to draw around 100,000. Strict 19+ — bring your passport.

items.title: Ezra Collective: First Headline Show in Korea
items.note: The London band that made jazz a Mercury Prize winner, playing Korea for the first time as headliners.
items.overview: Ezra Collective came out of the same London scene as Sons of Kemet and Nubya Garcia and took it further than anyone expected — 'Where I'm Meant To Be' won the Mercury Prize in 2023, the first jazz record ever to do so. Live they play closer to a party than a recital, pulling in afrobeat, grime and reggae. This is their first headline date in Korea, in a 1,000-capacity room.
items.ticketInfo: YES24 Ticket.
items.tip: YES24 Live Hall is by Gwangnaru Station on Subway Line 5, about five minutes' walk. It is a standing-first venue — the seated tier is on the balcony.

items.title: 10CM Fan Concert: The Missing Tracks
items.note: Three nights from the Korean singer-songwriter whose ballads keep turning up on drama soundtracks.
items.overview: 10CM is Kwon Jung-yeol, working solo under the name since 2017, and one of the few Korean acoustic acts whose songs cross over to listeners who do not follow K-pop — "Where Is Dream" from the Goblin soundtrack is the usual entry point. A fan concert is a looser, chattier format than a tour show, but the playing is the same and the room is small enough to hear it.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: Ages 7 and over. Olympic Park is on Subway Line 5 (Olympic Park Station) or Line 9 (Hanseong Baekje). Expect long Korean-language talk segments between songs — it is a fan event.

items.title: AKMU Concert: Paradise of Rumors
items.note: The beloved sibling duo across three arena nights — songwriting and sing-alongs over idol spectacle.
items.overview: AKMU (Akdong Musician) is the brother-and-sister duo of Lee Chan-hyuk and Lee Su-hyun, beloved across every Korean generation for their songwriting and Su-hyun's crystalline voice on hits like 'How People Move' and 'Love Lee.' These three KSPO Dome nights lean on musicianship and sing-along warmth rather than light-stick spectacle — a good pick if you want Korean pop beyond the idol format.
items.showTimes: Oct 9 (Fri) 6:00 PM · Oct 10 (Sat) 5:00 PM · Oct 11 (Sun) 4:00 PM KST
items.ticketInfo: Yes24 Ticket (English/global page available)
items.tip: KSPO Dome is inside Olympic Park (Subway Line 5/9). This is a lyrics-forward, emotional show — worth a quick listen to a few AKMU songs beforehand to get the most out of it.

items.title: GHOST Festival 2026 — Gyeonggi Hallyu OST Festival
items.note: Three days of K-drama soundtrack music, staged at the peace park beside the DMZ.
items.overview: GHOST is built around hallyu OST — the ballads and theme songs from Korean dramas, performed live by the singers who recorded them. The 2026 bill includes Yoon Do-hyun, Lee Mu-jin, Lee Seok-hoon and Hong Isaac among others. What makes it worth the trip is the setting: Imjingak Peace Nuri Park sits on the edge of the Civilian Control Line in Paju, a few kilometres from the DMZ, so the festival grounds are the same fields visitors normally see on a day tour.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through KREAM rather than the usual ticketing sites.
items.tip: All ages. Paju is about an hour and a half from central Seoul and public transport thins out in the evening — most people drive or take a shuttle. If you were planning a DMZ day trip anyway, this stacks the two.

items.title: BANG YONGGUK World Tour: HAEBANG
items.note: The former B.A.P leader, now making hip-hop on his own terms, in a 200-capacity basement.
items.overview: Bang Yongguk led B.A.P through the group's run and the legal fight that ended it, and has spent the years since making darker, more personal hip-hop as a solo artist. The HAEBANG tour plays small rooms deliberately — this Seoul date is in a basement venue holding a couple of hundred people, which for an artist with an international fanbase this size is unusual.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL). Tiered packages go up to a meet-and-greet.
items.tip: Ages 11 and over. Hyundai Card Understage is by Itaewon Station on Subway Line 6 — the venue is underground and standing-only.

items.title: Jarasum Jazz Festival in Gangneung
items.note: The Jarasum jazz programme on the east coast, with an international bill and a ₩20,000 ticket.
items.overview: Jarasum Jazz is Korea's best-known jazz festival, and this is its Gangneung edition — indoors at the Gangneung Arts Center rather than on the island in Gapyeong. The 2026 bill brings in Camille Bertault and Alfredo Rodríguez among others, which is a serious international lineup for the price. At ₩20,000 a ticket it is one of the cheapest ways to see musicians of this level anywhere.
items.ticketInfo: Booked directly through Gangneung Arts Center.
items.tip: Ages 7 and over. Gangneung is about two hours from Seoul on the KTX and the arts centre is a short taxi from the station. Mid-October is also when the east coast starts turning — the autumn colour guide has the timings.

items.title: tripleS World Tour: ANDLESS — Seoul
items.note: The 24-member 'decentralized' girl group in a compact central-Seoul arena — and famously affordable tickets.
items.overview: tripleS is a 24-member girl group under MODHAUS, billed as the world's first 'decentralized' idol group: instead of a fixed lineup, members rotate through sub-units whose makeup is shaped partly by fans through the Cosmo app and its digital photocards. The ANDLESS world tour opens in Seoul before heading to Macau, Tokyo and North America. Notably, MODHAUS priced the S-seat at just 30,000 won — a deliberate discount against rising K-pop ticket costs — and the Seoul shows sold out fast. Jangchung Gymnasium is a compact ~4,500-seat arena in central Seoul, so sightlines are closer than at the big domes.
items.ticketInfo: Ticketlink (Korean-language platform) — no confirmed English page for the Seoul dates; may require a Korean phone number to register
items.tip: Jangchung Gymnasium is on Subway Line 3 (Dongguk University Station) in central Seoul. Booking is the hard part: Ticketlink is Korean-only and usually needs phone/ID verification — set up a verified account well ahead, or catch the tour at an overseas stop.

items.title: Charlie Puth: Whatever's Clever! — Seoul
items.overview: Charlie Puth is an American singer-songwriter and producer known for polished pop hits like 'Attention,' 'We Don't Talk Anymore' and 'See You Again.' This Goyang stadium date, part of his 'Whatever's Clever!' world tour, is his return to Korea after about two years — a hit-driven pop show for a performer popular with Korean audiences.
items.ticketInfo: NOL Ticket / Live Nation Korea — English via NOL World and livenation.kr/en (limit 4 per person)
items.price: Roughly 99,000–785,000 won across seating tiers and VIP packages
items.tip: Same venue as The Weeknd (Goyang Stadium), well outside central Seoul — budget about an hour each way from downtown and expect crowded transport after the show.
items.note: Back in Korea after roughly two years, with a hit-driven pop set at the same Goyang stadium The Weeknd plays four nights earlier.

items.title: T-SQUARE Live in Seoul
items.note: Japanese fusion veterans, back in Seoul after seven years.
items.overview: T-SQUARE have been playing instrumental fusion since 1978, and their reach outside Japan owes a lot to video games and motorsport broadcasting — "Truth" has been the F1 theme in Japan for decades. This is their first headline Seoul date in seven years, in a seated university hall.
items.ticketInfo: NHN Ticketlink.
items.tip: Ages 8 and over. The Yonsei campus is a ten-minute walk from Sinchon Station on Subway Line 2 — Hongdae is one stop further if you want somewhere to go afterwards.

items.title: UNDERCITY presents Bart Skils
items.note: The Amsterdam techno DJ, a Drumcode mainstay, returns to Seongsu's UNDERCITY club for a Friday night. 19+.
items.overview: Bart Skils, one of the core artists on Adam Beyer's Drumcode label and a fixture of Amsterdam techno, plays UNDERCITY in Seongsu-dong a year after his last visit. Known for tracks like 'Your Mind' with Beyer, 'Roll the Dice' and 'YKSI', his sets are driving, hypnotic and built around long builds. Doors at 9 PM on a Friday; tiered tickets from 33,000 won in advance to 50,000 won on the door. Age 19 and over with ID.
items.ticketInfo: Advance tiers online; door sales 50,000 won
items.price: 33,000–44,000 won in advance · 50,000 won at the door
items.tip: UNDERCITY is in the Seongsu warehouse district, near Seongsu Station (Line 2). Bring a passport — clubs in Korea check ID at the door for anyone who looks under 30.

items.title: HIGHLIGHT Fan Con 2026
items.note: Three nights from one of the longest-running groups in K-pop, eighteen years in and still selling out an arena.
items.overview: Highlight are the four remaining members of the group that debuted as BEAST in 2009 — Yoon Doo-joon, Yang Yo-seob, Lee Gi-kwang and Son Dong-woon — and they are one of very few second-generation K-pop acts still touring as a unit. A fan concert is a looser format than a full tour show: more talking, more games, and a set that leans on the catalogue rather than a new album.
items.showTimes: Oct 16 (Fri) 7:30 PM · Oct 17 (Sat) 5:00 PM · Oct 18 (Sun) 4:00 PM KST · about 2h 30m
items.ticketInfo: YES24 Ticket. Fan-club presale usually takes most of the stock, so watch for the general round.
items.tip: Ages 6 and over. Jangchung Arena is at Dongguk University Station on Subway Line 3, Exit 1. Expect a lot of Korean-language talk segments — it is a fan event, not a concert with subtitles.

items.title: Lee Chang-sub Solo Concert: Unknown
items.venue: Grand Peace Palace, Kyung Hee University
items.note: BTOB’s main vocalist opens his solo tour with three nights in Seoul before Busan, Goyang, Suwon, Jeonju, Daegu and Ulsan.
items.overview: Lee Chang-sub is one of the strongest vocalists of his K-pop generation, a member of BTOB since 2012 and a musical-theatre lead in his own right. Unknown is his solo concert tour, opening with three nights at Kyung Hee University’s Grand Peace Palace, a 4,500-seat hall known for its acoustics, before visiting six more cities through November and December.
items.showTimes: Oct 16 (Fri) 7:30 PM · Oct 17 (Sat) 6:00 PM · Oct 18 (Sun) 5:00 PM KST
items.ticketInfo: Ticketlink — global site at global.ticketlink.co.kr
items.price: Soundcheck VIP 187,000 · R 165,000 · S and restricted view 154,000 won
items.tip: Hoegi Station (Line 1 and Gyeongui–Jungang), then a 15-minute walk or the campus bus; the hall is at the top of the hill.

items.title: Grand Mint Festival
items.note: Seoul's mellow, picnic-style autumn indie festival since 2007 — Younha, CNBLUE, Roy Kim, Jang Ki-ha and more.
items.overview: The Grand Mint Festival (GMF) is Seoul's signature autumn indie and acoustic festival, held every October at Olympic Park since 2007. Its character is deliberately mellow — indie, band sound, acoustic and singer-songwriter pop rather than the EDM or hip-hop of summer festivals — with a relaxed, picnic-like mood as crowds spread across the park's lawns and lakeside in crisp fall weather, across four stages. The 2026 lineup spans Younha, CNBLUE, N.Flying, Roy Kim, Jang Ki-ha, Peppertones, Thornapple and many more. It's a genuinely local, low-key event that rewards visitors who come for the music and the setting.
items.showTimes: Oct 17 (Sat) & Oct 18 (Sun) — timetable published in late September
items.ticketInfo: NOL, Yes24 Ticket, Naver Reservation (domestic); English booking via NOL World (world.nol.com)
items.price: 1-day pass 132,000 won (single-day tickets only — no 2-day pass)
items.tip: Book through the English NOL World page. Dress for cool mid-October evenings and bring or rent a picnic mat — much of the day is spent relaxing on the lawns between stages. Olympic Park is on Subway Line 5/9.

items.title: ILLIT Live: PRESS START — Encore
items.note: HYBE's fast-rising 5th-gen girl group (of 'Magnetic' fame) in a full arena encore next to Incheon Airport.
items.overview: ILLIT is a five-member girl group (Yunah, Minju, Moka, Wonhee, Iroha) formed through the 2023 survival show 'R U Next?' under BELIFT LAB, a HYBE label. Their 2024 debut single 'Magnetic' became a global viral hit, an unusually fast overseas breakthrough for a rookie act. These Incheon dates are the encore of their first concert tour — a genuine arena show (not a fan meeting), added after the original run sold out across Seoul, Japan and Hong Kong.
items.showTimes: Oct 17 (Sat) & Oct 18 (Sun) — start times to be announced
items.ticketInfo: Announced on ILLIT's Weverse; international booking via NOL World (world.nol.com). Prices to be confirmed.
items.tip: Set up your NOL World (English) account and finish passport verification before tickets open — ILLIT shows sell out fast. Bonus: INSPIRE Arena sits next to Incheon Airport, so it pairs well with an airport-area hotel on arrival or departure.

items.title: NOL Festival 2026
items.note: A two-day, multi-stage festival at KINTEX — and the K-pop and EDM stages are free.
items.overview: NOL Festival runs across two days and several stages at the KINTEX exhibition halls in Ilsan, splitting a K-pop stage, an EDM stage and a general live stage. The unusual part is the price: the K-pop and EDM stages are ticketed but free, which for a festival of this size is rare in Korea. Free does not mean walk-in — you still need to claim a ticket in advance, and they go.
items.showTimes: Oct 17 (Sat) from 4:00 PM · Oct 18 (Sun) — check each stage separately
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL). Each stage is ticketed separately; the K-pop and EDM stages are free but must be reserved.
items.price: K-pop and EDM stages free · other stages priced separately
items.tip: Ages 15 and over for the EDM stage. KINTEX is quickest on the GTX-A line from Seoul Station; the Line 3 route to Daehwa takes over an hour. Claim free tickets as soon as they open — they are the first thing to go.

items.title: Omoinotake One Man Tour in Seoul
items.note: The Japanese trio whose 'Ikuoku Kounen' broke out well beyond Japan, in a small Seoul hall.
items.overview: Omoinotake are a piano-led three-piece from Shimane — Hironoshin Tomita, Reo Fujii and Tomoaki Fukushima — who spent years on the live circuit before 'Ikuoku Kounen' turned them into a streaming fixture across Asia. The arrangement is unusual for a band this size: keys rather than guitar carry most of it.
items.ticketInfo: YES24 Ticket.
items.tip: All ages. The venue is in Sindang, by Cheonggu Station on Subway Lines 5 and 6 — the tteokbokki alley is a short walk and stays open late.

items.title: Paul Gilbert: WROC World Tour
items.note: The Mr. Big and Racer X guitarist, playing a 150-capacity room in Hongdae.
items.overview: Paul Gilbert has been one of the reference points for technical rock guitar since Racer X in the 1980s, and Mr. Big made him famous well beyond guitar circles — "To Be With You" was a worldwide number one. He tours small venues by choice and the shows are part concert, part masterclass. The room here holds about 150 people.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through 29CM rather than the usual ticketing sites.
items.tip: Ages 7 and over. Musinsa Garage is in Hongdae, a few minutes from Hongik University Station on Line 2 and the Airport Railroad. Standing-only and it will be full of guitarists.

items.title: Kenny G Live in Seoul
items.note: Two nights from the best-selling instrumental musician in history — and a fixture of Korean coffee shops for thirty years.
items.overview: Kenny G has sold more records than any instrumentalist alive, and in Korea specifically his catalogue occupies a strange cultural position: "Going Home" is played in shops, subway stations and department stores at closing time, so much so that most Koreans recognise it as the sound of the day ending rather than as a saxophone record. Two nights in a mid-size university hall.
items.ticketInfo: NHN Ticketlink.
items.tip: Ages 12 and over. The venue is on the Kwangwoon University campus in Nowon, north-east Seoul — Subway Line 1 or 7 to Seokgye Station.

items.title: Jannabi Ballad Collection: On a Fine October Day
items.note: A one-night, ballads-only Jannabi show at Olympic Park — the quieter side of the band, the night before their tour finale.
items.overview: A stand-alone Friday-night concert in which Jannabi set aside the rock numbers and play their ballads, the slow, orchestral side of their catalogue that made songs like 'For Lovers Who Hesitate' national favourites. Singer Choi Jung-hoon and guitarist Kim Do-hyung lead the band at Olympic Park in southeast Seoul. Tickets are 139,000 to 178,000 won; age 6 and over. Their Asia tour finale follows at the same venue on 24 and 25 October.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the official announcement for the outlet and hall
items.tip: Olympic Park Station (Line 5) or Hanseong Baekje Station (Line 9). Check your ticket for the hall name.

items.title: Joshua Redman Quartet in Seoul
items.note: One of the great tenor saxophonists of his generation, in an 800-seat hall.
items.overview: Joshua Redman has been one of the leading saxophonists in jazz since the 1990s, equally at home in straight-ahead quartets and in more contemporary projects. He brings his quartet to Yonsei University’s Centennial Hall, an intimate room for a player of his standing.
items.ticketInfo: Ticketlink — global site at global.ticketlink.co.kr
items.tip: Sinchon Station (Line 2). The Centennial Hall is inside the main gate on the left, well before the auditorium.

items.title: 82MAJOR 6th Concert — 82CLUB: out of control
items.note: The rising six-member boy group play two nights at YES24 Live Hall in Gwangjang-dong.
items.overview: 82MAJOR, a six-member boy group that has grown a fast international following since debuting in 2023, hold their sixth concert, titled 82CLUB: out of control, at YES24 Live Hall in eastern Seoul. The hall holds a couple of thousand people, so the shows are close-up by K-pop standards. All tickets are 132,000 won; age 7 and over.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the official announcement for the outlet
items.tip: YES24 Live Hall is a short walk from Gwangnaru Station (Line 5).

items.title: Jannabi Asia Tour Final: Sweat and Stardust — Seoul
items.note: Korea's best-loved retro-rock band close their Asia tour with two big Seoul nights at Olympic Park.
items.overview: Jannabi, the band whose 70s-flavoured rock and singer Choi Jung-hoon's theatrical delivery made them one of Korea's biggest live acts, wrap up their Asia tour with a two-night finale at Olympic Park in southeast Seoul. Expect a full-production arena show and a crowd that sings every word. Tickets run from 139,000 to 189,000 won; age 6 and over. The night before, on 23 October, the band also plays a separate ballad-only concert at the same venue.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the official announcement for the outlet and hall
items.tip: Olympic Park is on Line 5 (Olympic Park Station) and Line 9 (Hanseong Baekje Station). Confirm which hall on your ticket — the park has several.

items.title: Benson Boone Live in Korea
items.note: The American singer whose 'Beautiful Things' was inescapable in 2024, on his first Korean date.
items.overview: Benson Boone went from posting covers to one of the biggest singles of 2024 in about two years, and the live show has become known for a physical, backflip-and-all performance style that does not come across on record. This is a single Monday night at KINTEX in Ilsan.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: All ages. KINTEX is quickest on the GTX-A line from Seoul Station — the older route via Line 3 to Daehwa takes well over an hour from the centre.

items.title: FLOW: NARUTO The Rock World Tour
items.note: The Japanese band behind more Naruto openings than anyone else, playing a set built entirely around them.
items.overview: If you watched Naruto in any language, you have heard FLOW — 'GO!!!', 'Re:member', 'Sign' and several more of the series' opening themes are theirs. This tour is explicitly the anime set: a rock band playing the songs that a generation associates with a specific title sequence. They have been together since the late 1990s and tour internationally on the strength of exactly this.
items.ticketInfo: YES24 Ticket.
items.tip: All ages. YES24 Live Hall is five minutes from Gwangnaru Station on Subway Line 5. A Wednesday night show finishing around 21:30 leaves plenty of time to get back into the centre.

items.title: Kiefer Live in Seoul
items.note: The Los Angeles pianist and beat-maker in a 200-capacity Hongdae room.
items.overview: Kiefer is a jazz-trained pianist and producer from Los Angeles whose warm, loose instrumental records sit between jazz and hip-hop beats. This is a small-room show in Hongdae, close to the audience — the kind of gig that sells out quickly.
items.ticketInfo: NOL Ticket (Interpark) — English booking via NOL World (world.nol.com)
items.tip: Standing, all ages. Hongik University Station (Line 2, Airport Railroad) and a 10-minute walk into Seogyo-dong.

items.title: MOMENT FESTA: ONEWE × B1A4
items.note: A joint one-night bill of the rock band ONEWE and veteran boy group B1A4 in western Seoul.
items.overview: MOMENT FESTA pairs ONEWE, the five-piece band whose members play their own instruments, with B1A4, the boy group active since 2011 and now a three-member act, for one Friday-night show at Sky Art Hall in Gangseo-gu. The two share a label, so expect collaborations as well as separate sets. Tickets are tiered from 77,000 to 110,000 won; age 6 and over.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the official announcement for the outlet
items.tip: Sky Art Hall is in Deungchon-dong, western Seoul — Deungchon Station (Line 9) is the nearest stop.

items.title: Nujabes Metaphorical Ensemble Live
items.note: A live ensemble performing the work of Nujabes — the producer whose Samurai Champloo scores became the template for a whole genre.
items.overview: Jun Seba, who recorded as Nujabes, died in 2010, but his catalogue has only grown since — the Samurai Champloo soundtracks and albums like 'Metaphorical Music' are the origin point for most of what gets filed under lo-fi hip hop today. This is a live ensemble performing that material with real instruments rather than a DJ set, which is a genuinely different experience from the records.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: All ages. The venue is inside the Mecenatpolis complex above Hapjeong Station (Subway Lines 2 and 6), which puts you a few minutes from Hongdae afterwards.

items.title: EXO PLANET #6: EXhOrizon — Seoul Encore
items.note: Second-generation royalty on a full-group arena run — three encore nights closing their sixth solo tour.
items.overview: EXO is one of K-pop's defining second-generation groups, and these three nights are the encore closing their sixth solo tour, EXO PLANET #6 'EXhOrizon,' which first opened at the same venue in April. A full-group arena run of this scale is a rare event, so expect one of the fastest sell-outs of the season. Members: Suho, Xiumin, Baekhyun, Chen, Chanyeol, D.O., Kai and Sehun.
items.showTimes: Nov 6 (Fri) 7:00 PM · Nov 7 (Sat) 6:00 PM · Nov 8 (Sun) 5:00 PM KST
items.ticketInfo: Melon Ticket, with a separate global page (pre-sale opened late August)
items.tip: Expect the fastest sell-out of the autumn — set up a Melon Ticket Global account in advance, and if general sale fails, watch for the official cancellation-ticket release. KSPO Dome is on Subway Line 5/9.

items.title: Kep1er Fan-Con Tour: RSVP — Seoul
items.note: The girl group formed on Girls Planet 999 hold a two-day fan concert at Yonsei University's hall in Sinchon.
items.overview: Kep1er, the girl group formed through the survival show Girls Planet 999, play a two-day fan concert at Yonsei University's Centennial Hall in Sinchon. Fan-cons mix performance with talk and fan-interaction segments, so they are more intimate than a full concert and popular with overseas fans who want to see the members up close. All seats are 154,000 won.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the official announcement for the outlet
items.tip: Sinchon Station (Line 2) is the closest stop; the hall is inside the Yonsei campus, a 10-minute walk uphill.

items.title: Korea Grand Music Awards (KGMA) 2026
items.note: The newest of the big K-pop award nights, two days at the Gocheok Sky Dome a week before the Melon Music Awards.
items.overview: The Korea Grand Music Awards is run by the sports and entertainment daily Ilgan Sports and reaches its third edition in 2026. It is split into two nights with different line-ups: an ‘Artist Day’ on Saturday 7 November and a ‘Music Day’ on Sunday 8 November. The announced line-up runs from ATEEZ, RIIZE, ITZY and TREASURE to KISS OF LIFE, KiiiKiii, Hearts2Hearts and tripleS, with band and trot acts as well. It is broadcast live on the ENA channel.
items.showTimes: Nov 7 (Sat) Artist Day · Nov 8 (Sun) Music Day — start times to be announced
items.ticketInfo: Announced by the organisers on the official site (kgma-is.com); check there for the ticketing platform and dates
items.tip: Each day has a different line-up, so check which night your artist is on before buying. Gocheok Sky Dome is by Guil Station on Subway Line 1.

items.title: My Chemical Romance — Seoul
items.overview: My Chemical Romance are the legendary American emo/rock band behind 'The Black Parade' and anthems like 'Welcome to the Black Parade' and 'Helena.' This is a rare Korea headline show on their Asia tour, at Paradise City near Incheon Airport (the date was moved here from an original April 2026 booking).
items.ticketInfo: Ticketlink (mainly Korean-language); international presale was handled via UALIVE — English support is more limited than the NOL/Live Nation shows
items.price: Standing 175,000 · Seat R 195,000 · Seat P 220,000 won
items.tip: The venue is a big plus for travelers — Paradise City sits beside Incheon Airport on Yeongjong Island, connected to Terminal 1 by the AREX airport railway and free shuttle. It's about an hour from central Seoul, so staying near the airport is easiest.
items.note: A rare Korea headline date for the emo standard-bearers, rescheduled to Paradise City — the venue sits beside Incheon Airport.

items.title: Park Jinyoung 1st Concert Tour: CODE# — Seoul
items.note: GOT7's Jinyoung, also a leading actor, opens his first solo concert tour with two nights at Jangchung Arena.
items.overview: Park Jinyoung, the GOT7 member who has built a parallel career as an actor, launches his first solo concert tour with two shows at Jangchung Arena, the compact indoor arena beside Namsan in central Seoul. It is a rare chance to see a first-generation-of-the-2010s idol in a venue this size, and GOT7's international fandom means English-speaking fans will be well represented. VIP tickets are 176,000 won and general seats 154,000 won; age 6 and over.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the official announcement for the outlet
items.tip: Jangchung Arena is right by Dongguk University Station (Line 3). Small arena, so most seats have a good view.

items.title: Touché Amoré: Stage Four 10 Year Anniversary
items.note: The Los Angeles post-hardcore band playing 'Stage Four' in full, ten years on, in a 150-capacity room.
items.overview: 'Stage Four' is Touché Amoré's 2016 record about the death of Jeremy Bolm's mother, and it is the album that moved them from a hardcore band to something people write about differently. Anniversary sets like this usually mean the record start to finish. The venue holds not much more than a hundred people, which for a band of this stature is remarkable.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through 29CM rather than the usual ticketing sites — worth checking early.
items.tip: Ages 11 and over. Musinsa Garage is in Hongdae, a few minutes from Hongik University Station on Line 2 and the Airport Railroad. It is standing-only and it will be full.

items.title: GLOBAL CALLING: CamelPhat
items.note: The Grammy-nominated UK house duo play a late-night set at Lion Super Club in Cheongdam. 19+.
items.overview: CamelPhat, the Liverpool house duo behind 'Cola' and 'Panic Room', headline the Global Calling series at Lion Super Club in Cheongdam-dong, Gangnam's upmarket clubbing strip. The set starts at 11 PM on Thursday 12 November and runs into the early hours of Friday. Early-bird tickets are 40,000 won and fast-track entry 60,000 won. Age 19 and over.
items.showTimes: Nov 12 (Thu) from 11:00 PM KST, into the early hours of Nov 13
items.ticketInfo: Advance tickets online; check the club's channels for later tiers
items.price: Early bird 40,000 won · Fast track 60,000 won
items.tip: Cheongdam Station (Line 7) is the nearest stop, but taxis are the practical way home at closing time. Dress codes are enforced at Cheongdam clubs.

items.title: CHANGMO: MONOLITH
items.venue: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts
items.note: A Korean rapper taking over the country’s grandest concert hall for three nights.
items.overview: CHANGMO is one of the biggest names in Korean hip-hop, the rapper and producer behind ‘Maestro’ and ‘METEOR’, which topped the charts in 2019 and made him a mainstream star. MONOLITH puts him on the main stage of the Sejong Center, the 3,000-seat hall on Gwanghwamun Square more usually home to orchestras and musicals — a statement booking for Korean hip-hop.
items.showTimes: Nov 13 (Fri) 7:30 PM · Nov 14 (Sat) 7:30 PM · Nov 15 (Sun) 5:00 PM KST
items.ticketInfo: Sejong Center website (sejongpac.or.kr)
items.tip: Age 11+. Gwanghwamun Station (Line 5), exit 1, comes up at the hall; Gyeongbokgung is next door if you want a palace before the show.

items.title: Jason Mraz — Seoul
items.overview: Jason Mraz is the Grammy-winning American singer-songwriter behind easygoing hits like 'I'm Yours,' 'Lucky' and 'I Won't Give Up.' This KINTEX date, part of his Asia 2026 tour, is an intimate, feel-good acoustic-pop show from a longtime Korea favorite.
items.ticketInfo: NOL Ticket — English via NOL World (world.nol.com)
items.tip: KINTEX is in Ilsan — take the GTX-A line to Kintex Station for the fastest trip, or Subway Line 3 to Daehwa Station. Allow extra travel time from central Seoul.
items.note: An acoustic-leaning evening from the ‘I’m Yours’ songwriter, in a standing-only hall at KINTEX in Ilsan.

items.title: Melon Music Awards 2026
items.note: One of the year's biggest K-pop nights — and, for the first time, a two-day event at Seoul's only domed stadium.
items.overview: The Melon Music Awards (MMA) is one of Korea's four biggest year-end K-pop award ceremonies, run by Kakao Entertainment and built on data from Melon, the country's leading streaming service, plus fan voting and expert judging. The 2026 edition is the 18th and, for the first time in its history, expands to a two-day event — effectively a large K-pop festival of major live performances and awards, themed 'Connect.' Attendance is by ticket purchase (not a lottery), and the venue is Korea's only domed stadium, inside Seoul.
items.showTimes: Nov 14 (Sat) & Nov 15 (Sun) — start times to be announced
items.ticketInfo: Melon Ticket, with an English 'Melon Ticket Global' site (m.globalticket.melon.com). Note: MMA fan voting on the Melon app is a separate awards mechanism, not how you get a seat.
items.price: Roughly 90,000–200,000 won (based on the 2025 edition; 2026 pricing to be confirmed)
items.tip: Set up a Melon Ticket Global account in advance — its English support and international-card acceptance avoid the paid-membership and Korean-phone hurdles of other platforms. Gocheok Sky Dome is on Subway Line 1, the most accessible of the big venues for visitors without a car.

items.title: Awesome Stage: N.Flying × Hi-Fi Un!corn
items.note: Two FNC idol bands on one bill in Busan — real instruments, K-pop scale.
items.overview: N.Flying are the FNC rock band behind ‘Rooftop’, which became a surprise chart hit years after release, and Hi-Fi Un!corn are the Korean-Japanese band formed through FNC’s audition show. Awesome Stage puts them on a joint bill at BEXCO, Busan’s exhibition centre in Haeundae — a good excuse for a Busan weekend.
items.ticketInfo: Ticketlink — global site at global.ticketlink.co.kr
items.tip: Centum City Station (Busan Line 2) is at the BEXCO door; Haeundae Beach is two stops away for the rest of the day.

items.title: VICTON Concert: 10: NOW
items.venue: Woonjeong Green Campus, Sungshin Women’s University
items.note: The group’s tenth-anniversary concert, two nights in north Seoul.
items.overview: VICTON debuted under Play M Entertainment in 2016 and are marking ten years with 10: NOW, a two-night anniversary concert. Expect a set that runs through the back catalogue for long-time fans, in a mid-sized hall of about a thousand seats.
items.ticketInfo: Ticketlink — global site at global.ticketlink.co.kr
items.tip: The Woonjeong Green Campus is in Mia-dong, Gangbuk — not the main Sungshin campus. Mia Station (Line 4) is the nearest; allow a short taxi or bus ride.

items.title: yung kai Asia Tour: stay with the ocean, i'll find you — Seoul
items.note: First Korea show for the bedroom-pop singer behind the viral hit 'blue' — a small standing venue in Hongdae.
items.overview: yung kai, the American singer-songwriter whose track 'blue' spread worldwide through short-form video, plays his first Korean show on his Asia tour. It is a standing show at Musinsa Garage in Hongdae, a mid-sized live house, on a Monday night. General standing is 99,000 won and a VIP meet-and-greet package is 224,000 won. The date was first listed at Myeonghwa Live Hall and later at Musinsa Garage on KOPIS, so confirm the venue on your ticket.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the promoter's announcement for the outlet
items.price: Standing 99,000 won · VIP meet & greet 224,000 won
items.tip: Musinsa Garage is a short walk from Hongik University Station (Line 2). Standing only — arrive early for a spot near the stage.

items.title: Kings of Convenience at Seoul Jazz Festival
items.venue: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts
items.note: The Norwegian duo in a seated hall on Gwanghwamun square — quiet music in the right room.
items.overview: Erlend Øye and Eirik Glambek Bøe have been making the same kind of record since 'Quiet Is the New Loud' in 2001: two acoustic guitars, two voices, nothing hurried. They have an unusually devoted following in Korea, and this date is part of the Seoul Jazz Festival's theatre series rather than an outdoor stage — a seated hall suits them far better.
items.ticketInfo: Melon Ticket.
items.tip: Ages 6 and over. The Sejong Center is on Gwanghwamun Square — Subway Line 5, Gwanghwamun Station, Exit 1 or 8. Gyeongbokgung is a ten-minute walk north, so an afternoon at the palace pairs with this neatly.

items.title: 5 Seconds of Summer: Everyone's a Star! — Seoul
items.overview: 5 Seconds of Summer are the Australian pop-rock band known for 'Youngblood,' 'She Looks So Perfect' and 'Amnesia.' This 'Everyone's a Star! World Tour' stop is their first Korea headline show in about nine years — an energetic, all-standing pop-rock concert.
items.ticketInfo: NOL Ticket (NOL Interpark) — English via NOL World (world.nol.com)
items.price: Standing S 143,000 · Standing R 154,000 won (VIP package 320,000)
items.tip: A fully standing show (no seats) — wear comfortable shoes and arrive early for a good spot. KINTEX Hall 1 is in Ilsan: GTX-A to Kintex Station or Line 3 to Daehwa.
items.note: The Australian pop-rock band’s Seoul stop on the Everyone’s a Star! tour — standing floor, no seated tiers.

items.title: SJF at the Theater: Christopher
items.venue: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts
items.note: The Danish singer who is a genuine star in Korea, two nights in the Seoul Jazz Festival’s theatre series.
items.overview: Christopher is a Danish pop singer whose ballads and romantic pop have made him far bigger in Korea than in most of Europe, with sell-out Seoul shows and collaborations with Korean artists. These two nights are part of SJF at the Theater, the Seoul Jazz Festival’s autumn series of seated concerts in the Sejong Center.
items.ticketInfo: Melon Ticket — global page at tkglobal.melon.com
items.tip: Gwanghwamun Station (Line 5), exit 1. Seated, so no need to arrive hours early.

items.title: Stacey Kent Live in Seoul
items.note: The American jazz singer in one of Seoul’s best new concert halls.
items.overview: Stacey Kent is an American jazz singer known for her light, precise voice and a repertoire that moves between the Great American Songbook, French chanson and bossa nova. She plays the LG Arts Center Seoul, the Tadao Ando-designed hall that opened in Magok in 2022, before a date in Ulsan.
items.ticketInfo: LG Arts Center website (lgart.com)
items.tip: Magongnaru Station (Line 9, Airport Railroad) — handy if you are staying near Gimpo or flying out the next day.

items.title: AKMU Concert: Paradise of Rumors — Daegu
items.note: AKMU's national tour plays two nights at EXCO, Daegu's convention centre.
items.overview: The Daegu stop of AKMU's Paradise of Rumors tour: two shows at EXCO in the north of the city. Lee Chan-hyuk writes and Lee Su-hyun sings, and their live shows are known for reworking familiar songs in unexpected styles. Standing tickets (age 12 and over) and VIP seats are 176,000 won, R seats 165,000 won. Other dates on the tour include Gangneung (Nov 7), Daejeon (Dec 5–6), Busan (Dec 19–20) and Gwangju (Dec 25).
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the official announcement for the outlet
items.tip: EXCO is a short taxi ride from Daegu Station or Dongdaegu KTX Station. Standing tickets are limited to age 12 and over.

items.title: MONSTA X World Tour: THE X: NEXUS (Encore)
items.note: The encore that closes MONSTA X’s world tour, back home at INSPIRE Arena by Incheon Airport.
items.overview: MONSTA X debuted under Starship Entertainment in 2015 and built one of K-pop’s strongest international followings, with US tours and English-language releases alongside their Korean work. THE X: NEXUS is their world tour; these two encore nights bring it back to Korea at INSPIRE Arena, the 15,000-capacity arena in the resort on Yeongjong Island next to Incheon Airport.
items.ticketInfo: NOL Ticket (Interpark) — English booking via NOL World (world.nol.com)
items.tip: INSPIRE is 15 minutes from Incheon Airport by the resort’s free shuttle but over an hour from central Seoul — book the shuttle bus back or stay at the resort.

items.title: SJF at the Theater: Diana Krall
items.venue: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts
items.note: The Canadian jazz pianist and singer, one night in the Seoul Jazz Festival’s autumn series.
items.overview: Diana Krall is the best-selling jazz singer of her generation, a pianist and vocalist with a string of Grammy-winning albums of standards and her own songs. She plays a single night on the Sejong Center’s main stage in the Seoul Jazz Festival’s SJF at the Theater series.
items.ticketInfo: Melon Ticket — global page at tkglobal.melon.com
items.tip: Gwanghwamun Station (Line 5), exit 1. A Sunday-evening show, so you can be back at the hotel by nine.

items.title: ELLEGARDEN: Bad For Education Tour II
items.note: Two nights from the Japanese band that made English-language punk rock work in Asia, and never really went away.
items.overview: ELLEGARDEN formed in Chiba in 1998 and sang mostly in English, which is part of why they travelled as well as they did — 'Riot on the Grill' and 'ELEVEN FIRE CRACKERS' are still reference points for Japanese rock abroad. They went on hiatus in 2008, came back a decade later, and have been touring steadily since. Two nights here, and the ticket price is unusually reasonable for an international act.
items.showTimes: Nov 28 (Sat) · Nov 29 (Sun), both 6:00 PM KST · about 1h 30m
items.ticketInfo: YES24 Ticket.
items.tip: Ages 6 and over. Gwangnaru Station, Subway Line 5. At ₩88,000 this is one of the cheapest international rock tickets on the autumn calendar.

items.title: Malcolm Todd: First Show in Korea
items.note: The Los Angeles indie-pop singer's Korean debut, at a standing venue in Yeongdeungpo.
items.overview: Malcolm Todd, the young Los Angeles singer-songwriter whose guitar-led indie pop found a big streaming audience, makes his first appearance in Korea with a midweek show at Myeonghwa Live Hall in Yeongdeungpo. Standing and seated tickets are both 121,000 won, with early-entry and acoustic-session VIP packages priced from 252,000 to 436,000 won. Age 15 and over.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the promoter's announcement for the outlet
items.price: Standing / seated 121,000 won · VIP packages 252,000–436,000 won
items.tip: Myeonghwa Live Hall is near Yeongdeungpo Station (Line 1) and Yeongdeungpo-gu Office Station (Lines 2 and 5). Age 15+.

items.title: THE VOICE: LEE SEUNG CHUL — 40th Anniversary Tour
items.note: Three nights from one of the defining voices of Korean rock and ballad, closing a 40th-anniversary tour that has crossed the country since July.
items.overview: Lee Seung-chul has been a fixture of Korean popular music since 1985, when he arrived as the vocalist of Boohwal — one of the bands that built Korean rock — before going solo at the end of the decade. Four decades on he is still touring arenas, and the voice that earned him the nickname cheonsang-ui moksori, the heavenly voice, is the entire point of the show. The anniversary tour opened in Cheongju in July 2026 and runs through Gwangju, Daejeon, Daegu, Incheon and Busan; these three nights at the KSPO Dome are the Seoul dates, staged with a full band and a production scaled to the arena. Expect a career-spanning set — the ballads that everyone in the room can sing back, and the rock material that made his name.
items.ticketInfo: Yes24 Ticket. There is no dedicated English booking page, and Korean ticketing usually requires a Korean phone number or identity verification — see our K-pop ticket guide for the ways around that.
items.tip: This is a Korean-language show for a domestic audience, with no subtitles or English support — worth knowing before you book. If you are going anyway, the KSPO Dome sits inside Olympic Park: Subway Line 5 to Olympic Park Station, or Line 9 to Hanseong Baekje Station. Early December in Seoul is properly cold, and the walk in from the station is exposed.

items.title: KANA-BOON: Critical Hit Parade — Asian Adventure
items.note: Japanese guitar rock with an anime pedigree — 'Silhouette' was a Naruto Shippuden opening, and it has outlived the show.
items.overview: KANA-BOON came out of Osaka in the early 2010s playing fast, melodic guitar rock, and 'Silhouette' — written as a Naruto Shippuden opening — became the song that carried them abroad. The live set is short, loud and built for a room this size rather than an arena.
items.ticketInfo: YES24 Ticket.
items.tip: Ages 7 and over. Gwangnaru Station, Subway Line 5. An early 6pm start means you are out by half past seven — easy to pair with dinner in Gwangjin or a trip back to Hongdae.

items.title: Khalid: It's Always Summer Somewhere — Seoul
items.overview: Khalid is the American R&B/pop singer known for smooth, laid-back hits like 'Location,' 'Young Dumb & Broke' and 'Talk.' This Seoul date, part of his 'It's Always Summer Somewhere' tour, is a mellow, vocal-driven indoor show at KINTEX.
items.ticketInfo: NOL Ticket / Live Nation Korea — English via NOL World and livenation.kr
items.tip: KINTEX Hall 10 is in the KINTEX 2 building, Ilsan — GTX-A to Kintex Station or Line 3 to Daehwa. It's a December show, so dress for cold weather during transit.
items.note: Grammy-nominated R&B from the ‘Location’ and ‘Talk’ singer, on a standing-only floor at KINTEX.

items.title: YUURI LIVE in Seoul
items.note: Two nights from the Japanese singer-songwriter behind 'Dry Flower', at the arena next to Incheon Airport.
items.overview: Yuuri built an audience busking and posting online before 'Dry Flower' became one of the defining Japanese songs of the early 2020s, and 'Betelgeuse' followed it onto every chart that mattered. He writes for other artists as well as himself, and the live set is built around the voice rather than spectacle. Two nights at INSPIRE Arena, the 15,000-capacity room attached to the resort complex beside Incheon Airport.
items.showTimes: Dec 5 (Sat) 6:00 PM · Dec 6 (Sun) 5:00 PM KST · about 1h 30m
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: INSPIRE is on Yeongjong Island next to the airport, not in Incheon city — an hour from central Seoul on the Airport Railroad plus a shuttle. If you are flying out the next morning it is unusually convenient; otherwise book a room on site or plan the trip back carefully.

items.title: FKJ: Tyber — Seoul
items.overview: FKJ (French Kiwi Juice) is a French multi-instrumentalist and producer who blends electronic music with jazz, soul, funk and R&B, celebrated for his one-man live-looping performances. This Seoul date, part of his 'Tyber' tour, is an immersive, improvisational live set rather than a straightforward DJ show.
items.showTimes: Dec 6 (Sun) — start time to be confirmed
items.ticketInfo: NOL Ticket (also on Yes24 Ticket) — English via NOL World; age 12+, limit 4 per person
items.tip: Same building as the Khalid show (KINTEX Hall 10) — GTX-A to Kintex Station is fastest from Seoul. A standing show in a busy December concert period, so arrive early.
items.note: French multi-instrumentalist Vincent Fenton playing live loops solo — the most improvised show on this list, and the cheapest.

items.title: Slowdive Live in Seoul
items.note: The shoegaze band that defined the sound, still touring with the original five-piece lineup.
items.overview: Slowdive formed in Reading in 1989, made 'Souvlaki' in 1993, were written off by the British press, split, and then found that an entire generation of guitar bands had spent thirty years trying to sound like them. The reunion has outlasted the original run, and 'everything is alive' (2023) is as good as anything in the catalogue. All five original members are on this tour — Neil Halstead, Rachel Goswell, Christian Savill, Nick Chaplin and Simon Scott.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: Ages 12 and over. KBS Arena is in Gangseo, west of the centre — Subway Line 9 to Yangcheon Hyanggyo, or Line 5 to Balsan. It is a genuinely loud show; the venue does not hand out earplugs.

items.title: Benny Sings Live in Seoul
items.note: The Dutch soft-pop and soul songwriter plays an intimate Hongdae live house in December.
items.overview: Benny Sings, the Amsterdam-based singer, producer and songwriter known for warm, jazz-tinged pop and collaborations across the indie and hip-hop worlds, plays a one-night Seoul show at Musinsa Garage in Hongdae. It is a small venue by touring standards, which suits his relaxed, keyboard-led sets. All tickets are 99,000 won.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the promoter's announcement for the outlet
items.tip: Hongik University Station (Line 2) is the nearest stop. Hongdae's bars and late-night food are on the doorstep for afterwards.

items.title: DOMi & JD BECK: Who Asked? Tour
items.note: Keys and drums, both barely in their twenties, playing faster than seems reasonable.
items.overview: DOMi Louna and JD Beck are a French-American keyboard-and-drums duo whose debut 'NOT TiGHT' arrived on Anderson .Paak's label and immediately divided people into those who thought it was a gimmick and those who had seen them live. The playing is genuinely extraordinary — dense, fast, and much funnier than instrumental jazz usually allows. A single night in a small Seoul hall.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: The venue is in Sindang, near Cheonggu Station on Subway Lines 5 and 6. Sindang's tteokbokki alley is a five-minute walk and stays open late — an easy dinner before or after.

items.title: wave to earth Seoul Concert
items.note: Three home-town nights from the Korean trio that has spent the last two years selling out rooms across the US and Europe.
items.overview: wave to earth are Kim Daniel, Shin Dongkyu and Cha Soonjong, playing a soft, jazz-inflected indie that found its audience almost entirely through streaming and almost entirely outside Korea first — "seasons" and "bad" travelled before anyone at home was paying attention. They now tour internationally more than domestically, which makes a three-night Seoul run something of an event. If you follow them from abroad, this is the show at home.
items.showTimes: Dec 18 (Fri) 8:00 PM · Dec 19 (Sat) 6:00 PM · Dec 20 (Sun) 5:00 PM KST
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: Ages 10 and over. Hwajung Gymnasium is on the Korea University campus — Subway Line 6 to Korea University Station, then about ten minutes uphill. December nights in Seoul are cold and the walk is exposed.

items.title: AKMU Concert: Paradise of Rumors — Busan
items.note: The sibling duo's national tour reaches Busan for two December nights at BEXCO in Haeundae.
items.overview: AKMU, the brother-and-sister duo Lee Chan-hyuk and Lee Su-hyun, bring their Paradise of Rumors tour to BEXCO in Busan's Haeundae district for two shows on the weekend before Christmas. Their songs mix folk-pop songwriting with playful arrangements and Su-hyun's clear vocals, and the shows draw an all-ages crowd. The same tour also stops in Gangneung (Nov 7), Daegu (Nov 21–22), Daejeon (Dec 5–6) and Gwangju (Dec 25). Standing and VIP tickets are 176,000 won, R seats 165,000 won.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the official announcement for the outlet
items.tip: BEXCO is next to Centum City Station (Line 2), a few stops from Haeundae Beach. A good excuse for a winter weekend in Busan.

items.title: Aosaka: kurayamisaka & parannoul
items.note: Japan's kurayamisaka and Korea's cult shoegaze act parannoul share a January bill in Hongdae.
items.overview: A double bill for shoegaze and emo fans: kurayamisaka, the Japanese band whose loud, melodic guitar rock has crossed over online, and parannoul, the anonymous Seoul bedroom-shoegaze project whose album 'To See the Next Part of the Dream' became an international word-of-mouth favourite and one of the most acclaimed Korean records of the decade. The show is at KT&G Sangsangmadang Live Hall, the basement venue in the heart of Hongdae, on a Saturday evening in January. Standing tickets are 88,000 won.
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the promoter's announcement for the outlet
items.tip: Hongik University Station (Line 2), exit 9, then a five-minute walk through the Hongdae pedestrian streets. Standing only.

items.title: Fujii Kaze: Prema World Tour
items.note: The Japanese singer-songwriter whose 'Shinunoga E-Wa' found a second life worldwide, playing Seoul's only domed stadium.
items.overview: Fujii Kaze writes and plays his own material at the piano, and the combination of that and a voice that carries has made him one of the few Japanese artists with a genuinely global streaming audience — 'Shinunoga E-Wa' broke out internationally years after release and pulled the rest of his catalogue with it. The Prema world tour brings him to Gocheok Sky Dome, which is indoors and heated; in January in Seoul that matters more than it sounds.
items.ticketInfo: Melon Ticket. Melon usually requires Korean identity verification — see our K-pop ticket guide for what overseas buyers can actually do.
items.tip: Gocheok Sky Dome is on Subway Line 1 at Guil Station, about five minutes' walk. It is a baseball stadium with a roof, so unlike an outdoor January show you will be warm — but bring layers for the walk back to the station.

items.title: Maroon 5 Live in Korea
items.note: Two decades of radio singles in one night — and one of the few major international shows on the calendar in January.
items.overview: Maroon 5 have been a fixture of pop radio since 'Songs About Jane' in 2002, and the live set leans on exactly what you would expect: 'This Love', 'Sunday Morning', 'Moves Like Jagger', 'Memories'. The Seoul date lands at KINTEX in Ilsan, the exhibition hall that doubles as the region's mid-size concert venue. January is the quietest month in the Korean concert calendar, so if your trip falls then, this is one of the few large-scale shows running.
items.ticketInfo: Interpark (NOL).
items.tip: Ages 12 and over. KINTEX is served by Daehwa Station on Line 3 plus a walk, or the GTX-A line which is much faster from central Seoul. A Wednesday 8pm start in Ilsan means the last trains back are tight — check before you commit.

items.title: Bruno Mars Live in Korea
items.note: Bruno Mars returns to the Seoul area for a multi-night stadium run at Goyang — eight dates listed across ten days in late May.
items.overview: Bruno Mars plays Goyang Stadium, the open-air stadium northwest of Seoul that hosts the capital's biggest international tours, for a run of shows between 21 and 30 May 2027. The KOPIS listing shows eight dates: Friday to Sunday on both weekends plus the Tuesday and Wednesday in between, all starting at 7:45 PM. Standing and seated tiers are on sale from 99,000 to 280,000 won. This is one of the largest pop bookings in Korea in 2027 and the kind of show that fills hotels in Goyang and northern Seoul, so book accommodation early if you are planning a trip around it.
items.showTimes: May 21–23, 25–26 and 28–30, 2027, all 7:45 PM KST (as listed on KOPIS)
items.ticketInfo: Sold through Korean ticket outlets — check the official Live Nation Korea announcement for the outlet and sale dates
items.tip: Goyang Stadium is on Seoul Subway Line 3 (Daehwa Station, about a 10-minute walk). Age 7 and over. With eight shows, weekday dates are usually the easiest to get.
